# midpoint_role (Resource)

A midPoint role (RoleType). Simple, business and service roles and metaroles are all roles; the archetype tells them apart.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The service the roles below grant access to.
resource "midpoint_service" "dev_k8s" {
  name      = "dev-k8s"
  archetype = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000329" # Application
}

# An application role granting access to the service.
resource "midpoint_role" "dev_k8s_admin" {
  name         = "dev-k8s / admin"
  display_name = "Dev cluster / admin"
  description  = "Administrator access to the dev cluster."
  identifier   = "admin"
  risk_level   = "high"
  archetype    = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000328" # Application role

  inducement {
    target {
      oid  = midpoint_service.dev_k8s.oid
      type = "ServiceType"
    }
  }
}

# A business role: induces another role found by a midPoint query, and
# creates an LDAP account for its members' members.
resource "midpoint_role" "platform_team" {
  name = "platform-team"

  inducement {
    target {
      type   = "RoleType"
      filter = "name = \"vault / operator\""
    }
  }

  inducement {
    order = 2
    construction {
      resource = "c5a3191b-89c7-479e-82b9-6093c60566f2"
      kind     = "account"
      intent   = "default"
    }
    condition = jsonencode(yamldecode(file("${path.module}/only-employees.yaml")))
  }

  extension = {
    costCenter = "CC-123"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Object name.

### Optional

- `activation` (Block, Optional) Activation. Other activation items (validity) go in extra. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--activation))
- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) When an object with the configured oid already exists, adopt it into state and apply the configuration to it as an update instead of failing. The configuration must describe the whole object: items midPoint holds that are not configured (other than server-managed ones) are removed on the first apply. The plan warns that the object will be adopted and lists the changes the update will send. Meant for the midPoint built-ins a catalogue customizes. Without it, creating an object whose oid already exists fails and nothing is written. While it is true, destroying the object fails unless force_destroy is set: an adopted object is not Terraform's to delete. Remove it from state with a removed block (lifecycle { destroy = false }) to stop managing it. Defaults to false.
- `archetype` (String) OID of the archetype, written as an assignment to it. On read that assignment is shown here (after an import, or when archetype was set); do not also write it as an assignment block.
- `assignment` (Block List) An assignment (membership, archetype, org). Values are matched to midPoint by content (target, construction, order), not by position. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment))
- `authorization` (Dynamic) Authorizations (authorization), a list in midPoint naming, e.g. [{ action = ["http://midpoint.evolveum.com/xml/ns/public/security/authorization-model-3#read"] }].
- `delegable` (Boolean) Whether its holders can delegate it.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `display_name` (String) Display name (displayName).
- `extension` (Dynamic) Schema extension items, e.g. { costCenter = "CC-123" }. Values are scalars or lists.
- `extra` (Dynamic) Other midPoint items, merged at the object root, in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. yamldecode(file("extra.yaml")). An item must not also be set by a typed attribute; assignment and inducement values here are added to the blocks (they hold the values a block cannot express).
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the object even while objects assigned to it or holding it in roleMembershipRef (members) exist. Without it, the delete fails and names the first few members. It also allows deleting an object adopted with adopt_existing = true, which is refused otherwise. Defaults to false.
- `identifier` (String) Identifier.
- `inducement` (Block List) An inducement: what holders of this object get. Values are matched to midPoint by content (target, construction, order), not by position. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--inducement))
- `lifecycle_state` (String) Lifecycle state (lifecycleState), e.g. active, draft, proposed.
- `oid` (String) Object OID. When unset midPoint generates one. Changing it replaces the object. Creating an object whose oid already exists fails unless adopt_existing is set.
- `options` (List of String) midPoint execution options sent on create and update, e.g. raw, isImport, reevaluateSearchFilters. When unset, the provider default_options entry for role applies, else the built-in defaults: isImport, raw on create and raw on update. An empty list sends no options. overwrite is sent only when listed here; reevaluateSearchFilters is added to any write that sends a reference with a filter and no oid.
- `requestable` (Boolean) Whether users can request it.
- `risk_level` (String) Risk level (riskLevel).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The object OID.

Optional:

- `administrative_status` (String) Administrative status (administrativeStatus): enabled, disabled or archived.


<a id="nestedblock--assignment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment`

Optional:

- `condition` (String) Condition (MappingType) as JSON text in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. jsonencode({...}) or jsonencode(yamldecode(file("x.yaml"))).
- `construction` (Block, Optional) Resource object construction. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment--construction))
- `extra` (String) Other items of this assignment (e.g. description, activation, focusType), an object, as JSON text in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. jsonencode({...}) or jsonencode(yamldecode(file("x.yaml"))).
- `order` (Number) Assignment order; 2 makes an inducement apply to the members of the members.
- `policy_rule` (String) Policy rule (policyRule) as JSON text in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. jsonencode({...}) or jsonencode(yamldecode(file("x.yaml"))).
- `target` (Block, Optional) The assigned or induced object, by oid, by filter, or both. At least one of oid and filter is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment--target))

<a id="nestedblock--assignment--construction"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment.construction`

Optional:

- `body` (String) Other construction items (attribute, association, ...), an object, as JSON text in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. jsonencode({...}) or jsonencode(yamldecode(file("x.yaml"))).
- `intent` (String) Object intent, e.g. default.
- `kind` (String) Object kind, e.g. account or entitlement.
- `resource` (String) Resource OID.


<a id="nestedblock--assignment--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment.target`

Optional:

- `filter` (String) midPoint text query selecting the target, e.g. name = "vault / operator". midPoint resolves it when the object is written; with a filter only, Terraform knows no dependency on the target, so ordering is up to the configuration.
- `oid` (String) Target object OID.
- `relation` (String) Relation of the reference, e.g. org:manager. Defaults to org:default. A name without a prefix is in the org: namespace, as midPoint stores it: manager is written org:manager.
- `type` (String) Target object type, e.g. RoleType, ServiceType, OrgType, ArchetypeType.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the object OID.
terraform import midpoint_role.dev_k8s_admin 40a44000-c0b6-45b9-bce4-9ad9d51fbf63
```
